messages:
Maria P: Quick sync — I'm reworking the console UX for automatic fallback policies; want to land something before next week's release.
Jordan H: 👍 do you mean the policy editor in the route page or a separate rollouts flow?
Maria P: Thinking separate rollout object that references routes. Debate: keeping fallback config in route gives immediate visibility, but makes route schema noisy.
Ben T: Route-level is simpler for ops. If fallback is a separate resource we need good linking and cross-filtering in Console.
Alisha K: One UX pain I keep hearing — users can't easily tell which fallback mode actually ran for a given request. Need clearer audit playback.
Sam L: We should capture the resolution chain: incoming route -> matched policy -> chosen fallback variant. Make it searchable.
Maria P: Agreed. Proposal A: route-level fallback toggle with inline compact editor. Proposal B: rollout-level policy with explicit canary + simulate toggles.
Jordan H: Also include trigger editor: right now it's opaque. e.g., "error_rate >= 5% over 1m" or "p95 latency > 800ms". Need friendly presets.
Alisha K: Presets would help. Also add a "dry-run" mode that routes traffic but tags telemetry, doesn't change path.
Ben T: For auditing we need immutable snapshots of the policy at the time of switch. Can't rely on current config when replaying events.
Maria P: Exactly. Audit requirements: snapshot+reason+actor. UI should show diff between active policy snapshot and current config.
Sam L: Telemetry-wise, we should annotate traces with the fallback decision and variant id, e.g., `fallback.variant_id=uuid`.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary job started for `fallback-ui-experiment` — 5% traffic to canary variant
Jordan H: One more API debate — should the SDK expose `applyFallback(route_id, policy)` vs `createRollout({targets:[route]})`? Implementation aligns with the model shape.
Alisha K: My vote is the latter: rollout as first-class. Easier to support canary, unroll, and audit timeline.
Ben T: But for small teams they want a single toggle on the route. Can we support both? route.fallback = { rollouts:[latest] }
Maria P: Supporting both increases complexity but could be helpful. UX: show route toggle that links to rollout editor if non-default.
Sam L: Also add a "why did we route to fallback" link in request log that opens the exact snapshot and the trigger metrics at that moment.
Maria P: I'll prototype a compact route-level card + full rollout editor. Mock will include: triggers presets, dry-run, snapshot timeline, telemetry tag example.
Jordan H: Can you add an optional "replay" action for admins that simulates the decision on historical trace with the snapshot?
Maria P: Yes — with guard: replay only on anonymized traces and must record replay audit event.
Alisha K: UX note: don't use scary language. call it "Fallback mode: graceful degrade" not "failover". Keep labels consistent.
Maria P: Good call. I'll update the copy. Thanks everyone — will post mockups tomorrow.
Ben T: Thanks — looped in infra team to check telemetry storage costs.
Maria P: tagging follow-ups: @Jordan H for API shape, @Sam L for telemetry tags, @Alisha K for wording and presets.
ops-bot: reminder: mobile-standup 10m
